name: DFRobot DFR0821 Fermion: DS3232 precise RTC breakout (I2C real time clock with 236 B battery-backed SRAM, CR1220 backup)
//: Catalog record written by /spark:research on 2026-09-29 — read, not chosen. Filled ONLY from what was actually read: DFRobot's wiki and product page, the schematic PDF (text layer plus a rendered image), the dimension drawing (rendered image; its PDF has no text layer), the DS3232 datasheet copy DFRobot host (grepped for the rows cited) and the DFRobot_DS323X library README. A null is a fact nobody has recorded. verified: true = the vendor's own text at the cited URL; read off an image, inferred or computed = false with why_it_matters.
//why_not: The DFR0819 with 236 bytes of battery-backed SRAM for $12.00; nothing in the irrigation brief needs the SRAM, and it shares the DFR0819's price gap against the chosen DFR0641.
//variant: True of the DFR0821 at PCB V1.0 — the drawing's silkscreen reads 'DS3232 Precise Real Time Clock V1.0', its table 'DFR0821[V1.0]' dated 20210413, and the schematic is V1.0 dated 2021-04-13. The chip on the schematic image is a DS3232SN# (industrial, -40 to +85 °C per the datasheet). Same 22.5 x 21 mm outline, hole pair and VCC·GND·SCL·SDA·INT·RST·32K row as the DFR0641 and DFR0819; like the DFR0819 its INT and 32K pull-ups are 10k, not the DFR0641's 100k.
//sources: The 'datasheet' DFRobot host is Maxim's DS3232 datasheet, 19-5337 Rev 5, 7/10 (19 pages), read only for the rows cited below. A second wiki slug (wiki.dfrobot.com/Fermion_DS3232_Precise_RTC_SKU_DFR0821) appeared in search results and was not opened.

needs.note: Pulled to the module's VCC by R4 10K on the module. The wiki's pinout table labels SDA 'I2C Clock line' and SCL 'I2C Data line' — swapped descriptions, as on the DFR0819's wiki; the schematic is unambiguous.
Pulled to the module's VCC by R3 10K on the module.
'Interrupt in low level or 1Hz square wave output' (wiki). Pulled to VCC by R2 10K on the module.

power.note: 'Power Supply Voltage: 3.3V-5.5V'. The pull-ups return to this pin, so it sets the bus's high level — feed it from the logic rail on a 3.3 V host. Decoupled on the module by C4 100nF.

unused_pins.note: 'Reset calibration pin' (wiki); runs straight from the chip's RST# pin to the pad with nothing else on the module (schematic image). The DS3232 datasheet copy was not read for this pin.
'32.768KHz Pulse Output' (wiki); net '32kHz' on the schematic, pulled to VCC by R1 10K.

//pin_order: Seven pads numbered 1..7 on the wiki's table (text) and the schematic's P1 'Header 7' (text layer): VCC GND SCL SDA INT RST 32K. The dimension drawing's silkscreen (image) reads the same top to bottom down the right-hand edge, VCC at the top — which physical end is pad 1 is therefore image-read, see pad_1_position.
//footprint: The host carries the mating seven-pad 2.54 mm row; the shipping list includes a '2.54-7P Black Single Row Connector x1'.

body_mm.where: 'Product Size: 22.5*21mm / 0.89*0.83 inch'; the dimension drawing (image) reads 22.50mm x 21.00mm
body_mm.note: Drawing (image, PDF has no text layer): two holes ø2.00 mm on the left edge 15.00 mm apart, the seven-pad row down the right edge, an SO-20 chip and six passives on top, no holder visible on top; PCB Information table: Thickness 1.0mm, Engineer HDJ, Date 20210413, black mask, white silkscreen.
body_mm.why_it_matters: every placement is arranged around it

i2c_address.where: Specification: 'I2C Address: 0x68'; the wiki says the same

chip_variant.where: U1 on the schematic IMAGE reads 'DS3232SN#' (the text layer gives only 'DS3232'); the datasheet lists commercial 0 to +70 °C and industrial -40 to +85 °C variants
chip_variant.why_it_matters: Decides the cold rating; DFRobot's product page says -40 to +85 °C, which matches the SN#.

sram_bytes.where: 'SRAM: 236 Byte (0x14~0x1F)'; the datasheet: '236 bytes of battery-backed SRAM'
sram_bytes.why_it_matters: The one thing this board has that the DFR0819 does not: a few bytes that survive a power cut on the cell — e.g. a watering log's last entry — without a host flash write.

timekeeping_accuracy_ppm.where: 'Timing Accuracy: ±3.5ppm (±0.3024 sec/day)'; the datasheet: ±2ppm from 0 to +40 °C, ±3.5ppm from -40 to +85 °C

backup_cell.where: 'The button cell model that goes with the module is CR1220'; 'does not come with batteries anymore'

cell_holder_on_board.where: BT1 on the VBAT net (text layer and image); the product page names the CR1220 it takes
cell_holder_on_board.why_it_matters: Not visible on the top-side drawing, so it is on the reverse — inferred, as for the DFR0641 — which decides whether the module can lie flat on a host.

cell_charged_by_module.where: on the schematic image VBAT connects to BT1, C1 100nF and the chip's VBAT pin only — no diode or resistor from VCC
cell_charged_by_module.why_it_matters: Fit a primary CR1220; a rechargeable LIR1220 would never be charged.

module_has_i2c_pullups.where: text layer: R3 10K, R4 10K beside VCC and the SCL/SDA lines; the image shows R3 on SCL and R4 on SDA, both to VCC
module_has_i2c_pullups.why_it_matters: The FireBeetle 2 ESP32-S3 V1.2+ has no I2C pull-ups of its own, so these are the bus's pull-ups unless another module brings its own.

i2c_pullup_ohms.why_it_matters: Same value as the DFR0641, so the same limit: at 10k alone a 400 kHz bus tolerates only a few tens of pF; a cable means 100 kHz or a parallel pull-up.

int_pullup_ohms.where: R1 10K, R2 10K (text layer); the image shows R2 on INT and R1 on 32kHz, both to VCC
int_pullup_ohms.why_it_matters: What an interrupt or wake input sees; not the DFR0641's 100k.

pullup_32khz_ohms.where: R1 10K (text layer), on the 32kHz net per the image

vbat_range_v.where: Recommended DC Operating Conditions: VBAT 2.3 min, 3.0 typ, 5.5 max (DS3232 datasheet 19-5337 Rev 5)

mounting_holes.value: 2 x ø2.00 mm on the left edge, 15.00 mm apart
mounting_holes.where: dimensioned on the drawing, but the PDF has no text layer so this is image-read: 'ø 2.00mm X2', '15.00mm'; the inset from the left edge is not dimensioned
mounting_holes.why_it_matters: What a host board or enclosure boss lines up with; the DFR0641's drawing dimensions the same pair as M2 at 2.5 mm from the edge.

pad_1_position.value: VCC is the top pad of the column on the right-hand edge
pad_1_position.where: silkscreen on the drawing image, VCC GND SCL SDA INT RST 32K top to bottom; no pad-1 marker is drawn
pad_1_position.why_it_matters: The generator numbers the row from pad 1; reversed, GND lands on VCC's pad.

pcb_thickness_mm.where: PCB Information table on the drawing image: 'Thickness: 1.0mm'
pcb_thickness_mm.why_it_matters: A socket's grip and standoff arithmetic; 1.0, not the usual 1.6.

library.where: README: 'SKU: DFR0641/DFR0819/DFR0821'; boards table lists FireBeetle-ESP32

host_requirements: Feed VCC from the 3.3 V logic rail, never the 5 V one: the module's 10k pull-ups tie SDA and SCL to its VCC, so VCC is the bus's high level.
Add no I2C pull-ups for this module; it brings 10k on each line. Count what every other module on the bus adds — they parallel — and set the bus speed to the result.

Fit a primary CR1220; the module charges nothing. The holder is not on the top side of the drawing, so it is on the reverse (inferred) and the module cannot lie flat on a host without a socket or standoffs.
Leave RST and 32K open unless the DS3232 datasheet has been read for them; both are brought straight to pads.

sourcing.stock: not stated on the page; ships without the CR1220
